draft.subject: Notes that hold up when the payer asks
draft.body:
You tried JotPsych once. You didn't buy, and that's fine — most people need to see a tool work before they trust it.

One thing worth knowing: JotPsych now runs 150+ payer rule checks on every note before it's finalized. It flags missing elements, weak medical necessity language, and coding mismatches — the things that trigger a documentation request or a denial three months later.

Works with any EHR. Or replaces it entirely. No migration required; you can add it to what you're using today and be up in five minutes.

If audit-ready documentation matters in your practice, it's worth a second look.

Nathan Peereboom
JotPsych

--

failures: judge: The draft states 'You tried JotPsych once. You didn't buy' as established fact, but the RECIPIENT RECORD only confirms 'they signed up for JotPsych at some point and did not become a paying customer.' The draft assumes they actively tried/used the product, which is not verified.
judge: The phrase 'audit-ready documentation matters in your practice' assumes facts about the recipient's practice priorities that are not in the RECIPIENT RECORD.

judge: The recipient's specialty is 'Case Manager/Care Coordinator' per the allowed_facts. This role typically does not write clinical notes subject to payer audits or handle CPT/ICD coding. The entire premise—payer rule checks, medical necessity language, coding mismatches, audit-ready documentation—is irrelevant to a case manager's workflow. This is a fundamental targeting failure that would immediately signal to the recipient that this is untargeted mass mail.
